newsitem.title: UK: EBRD sets up $30 mln Russian equity fund.
newsitem.headline: EBRD sets up $30 mln Russian equity fund.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has set up a $30 million equity fund to modernise and restructure new enterprises in Russia's Black Earth region, the bank said in a statement.

The bank said the equity fund would be the eleventh and final fund in the Regional Venture Fund (RVF) programme and technical assistance worth $20 million would also be provided by the European Union's TACIS programme to develop the region.
"This marks the conclusion of the establishment phase of the RVF programme," Sven Hegstad, director of the EBRD's Early Stage Equity team, said in the statement.
"Our objective is to help privatised and new enterprises modernise and restructure through equity investments, active corporate governance and technical assistance," he said.
To manage the RVF a consortium had founded the Rabo Black Earth Regional Venture fund under the management of the Dutch Rabobank International.
Other consortium members include the Dutch investment consultancy, EWIC/Larive and Flemish investment company GIMV, said the statement.

The activity of the Rabo Black Earth venture fund would concentrate on Belgorod, Kursk, Lipetzk, Tambov and Voronezh, an area which lies 600 kilometres south of Moscow and considered one the most fertile in the world.

The bank said the EBRD's 10 regional venture funds in Russia had approved 24 investments worth ECU 14.6 million, of which 11 were signed and five were disbursing. A total of 13 investments should be approved in the next six months.
